keyVerseText: This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the LORD God of Israel had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the LORD his God upon him.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew adjective מָהִיר (mâhîyr) derives from the root מָהַר (mâhar), which fundamentally conveys the idea of hastening or making haste. This root suggests not only swiftness but also a readiness and promptness in action, implying a flow or movement that is smooth and unimpeded. Beyond the common English glosses like 'quick' or 'hasty,' the root sense emphasizes an active preparedness and skillfulness that accompanies speed, reflecting a deliberate and efficient readiness rather than mere impulsiveness.
usageInScripture: The word מָהִיר appears four times in the Hebrew Scriptures, consistently conveying a sense of promptness, diligence, or readiness. Its translations include 'and he was a ready,' 'of a ready,' 'diligent,' and 'and hasting,' demonstrating a semantic range that centers on both swiftness and competence. This consistency reveals that the term emphasizes not only quickness but also the skill and preparedness that accompany prompt action, highlighting a positive attribute of being both ready and capable.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מָהִיר as denoting both readiness and skill enriches our grasp of biblical characters and qualities esteemed by God. It underscores the value of being prepared and diligent in service to the Lord, reflecting a faithful response to His calling. This readiness is not rashness but a disciplined, God-empowered promptness that equips believers to act in accordance with divine justice and wisdom. Such a trait aligns with the Christian call to be watchful and ready, embodying a faith that is active and responsive to God's leading.
keyVerseReflection: In Ezra 7:6, the description of Ezra as a 'ready scribe' in the law of Moses highlights מָהִיר as denoting not only his promptness but his skill and preparedness in handling God's Word. This readiness enabled Ezra to fulfill his God-given task effectively, with the king granting his requests as a result of the Lord's favor upon him. The word thus enriches the verse by portraying Ezra as a diligent and capable servant, prepared to enact God's will with both speed and competence.
